newsitem.title: CANADA: Spar stock drops further on lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Spar stock drops further on lawsuit.

text.p: Shares in Spar Aerospace Ltd declined further on Wednesday amid investor concerns about a lawsuit filed in the United States against the Canadian space and communications equipment maker.
Spar stock fell 0.55 to 10.15 in light trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange today after dropping 18 percent from its close of 12.25 on Friday when the suit was filed. Spar's 52-week high was 16.30.
The lawsuit, filed by 14 firms in Los Angeles County, alleged that Spar's communications technology malfunctioned on a satellite used by American Mobile Satellite Corp.
The consortium said that Spar knew of a defect but did not do anything. The group said its insurance firms paid AMSC US$66 million for damages.
Spar denies the allegations in the suit. Spar spokeswoman Deborah Allan said Spar was considering a countersuit but that the legal battle could drag on for years.

Allan said there were two claims in the suit - one for US$66 million to cover the damages, and a second for US$69 million for lost revenues. Spar's lawyers believed the claims were overlapping and that the suit was worth US$69 million, she said.
Yorkton Securities analyst John Drolet called the suit "a most unfortunate development."
"There is a possibility that Spar will be hit with (the costs)," Drolet said.

An analyst who declined to be identified said investors had assumed the worst and had priced in most of the suit's costs at up to C$2 a share. But more important, said the analyst, was that Spar's reputation could suffer until the suit was settled.

"It doesn't help their reputation going forward and in generating additional business in this area, so the reputational issue is probably more damaging than the... C$1.80 to C$2 charge that otherwise might be taken if they were shown to be guilty," he said.
The stock would likely hover around its current price until further developments, Drolet said.
Spar, which is seeking to sell its ComStream communications unit, earned C$0.03 a share in the first quarter, versus a year earlier loss of C$0.34 a share.
